extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in undergraduate mathematics education (instructors of differential equations)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical evaluation of an Inquiry-Oriented Differential Equations (IO-DE) instructional approach that leverages Realistic Mathematics Education and social negotiation to teach undergraduate differential equations, compared to more conventional approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students' beliefs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study included students’ beliefs as an outcome dimension to compare IO-DE classes with more conventional approaches. (Abstract lists beliefs alongside skills and understandings as measured outcomes.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Students' skills (routine skills)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The main results reported no significant difference between IO-DE project students and comparison students on an assessment of routine skills; implies routine procedural competence is an explicit evaluation dimension when assessing instructional approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students' conceptual understanding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found a significant difference in favor of project (IO-DE) students on an assessment of conceptual understanding; conceptual understanding is therefore an explicit and important metric for evaluating instructional designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry-oriented instruction (IO-DE)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IO-DE approach itself is presented as the instructional intervention: an inquiry-oriented approach applied to undergraduate differential equations. Evaluation compares IO-DE to conventional instruction to judge its effects on beliefs, skills, and understandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional design theory: Realistic Mathematics Education
rubrics_metrics.description: the instructional design theory of Realistic Mathematics Education
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IO-DE is described as capitalizing on advances including Realistic Mathematics Education (RME); RME principles are therefore a design criterion for the curriculum/activities underlying IO-DE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social negotiation of meaning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The approach draws on the social negotiation of meaning as a theoretical/pedagogical underpinning, indicating collaborative discourse, classroom norms, and sociomathematical practices are evaluative/design considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evaluation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: comparison of students’ beliefs, skills, and understandings in IO-DE classes to more conventional approaches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses a comparative study design with assessments (routine skills, conceptual understanding, beliefs) and reports statistical significance; thus an appropriate rubric includes clear outcome measures, comparison groups, and statistical evaluation of differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability / relevance to undergraduate reform
rubrics_metrics.description: the theoretical underpinnings of the innovative approach may be useful more broadly for undergraduate mathematics education reform
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One criterion for judging an instructional innovation is whether its theoretical foundations and observed effects suggest it is useful and scalable for broader undergraduate mathematics education reform.
